name: an impulse

VINIT.justification: The baseline electrochemical gradient before stimulus arrival

TANCH.justification: The return to baseline that closes the event window

AFWD.justification: The movement toward the threshold of excitation

AREV.justification: The movement toward repolarization and descent from the peak

CLINK.justification: The sequential chain of segment deploarizations

IMSCRIB.justification: The voltage level where the channel recognizes its own state to trigger opening

FSPLIT.justification: The division of the pulse into an active transmission branch and a metabolic cost branch

FFUSE.justification: The reunification of signal and metabolic recovery into a completed pulse

EVALT.justification: Successful generation of the all or none spike

EVALF.justification: Failure to reach the firing threshold

ENGAGR.justification: A state where the neuron is both excited and inhibited simultaneously

IFIX.justification: The permanent chemical trace left by the impulse passage

phase_3.void_description: The silent synapse before neurotransmitter binding
phase_3.true_description: The binary 1 of a successful discharge spike
phase_3.false_description: The binary 0 of a graded potential that failed to fire
phase_3.both_description: The interference pattern of simultaneous EPSP and IPSP signals

steps.domain_action: Initialization of the resting potential at negative seventy millivolts
The membrane monitors its own voltage state to detect fluctuations
The stimulus initiates a positive voltage shift toward the threshold
The membrane evaluates whether the depolarization meets requirements
The threshold is surpassed leading to the primary firing arm
Rapid opening of sodium channels in a sequential chain reaction
The peak voltage is reached and recorded as a discrete event
Potassium channels open to initiate the downward phase
The recovery phase joins the signal completion to finalize the cycle
The system enters a second sub-decision for immediate re-firing
The absolute refractory period prevents any immediate new impulse
The relative refractory period permits firing only with high intensity
The period of instability resolves into a single recovery state
The pump restores original ion concentrations and seals the event

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Voltage gated ion channel protein structures
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Vesicle depletion and long term potentiation state
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Biological clock and local circuit refractory timers
phase_5.alfs_store: The genetic encoding for channel density and type

phase_6.cycle_cost: Adenosine triphosphate for sodium potassium pump operation
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Restored ordered electrochemical gradient after dissipation
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — Metabolic energy expenditure maintains the gradient order over the cycle
